life_summary: Dale Grant Renlund was born on November 13, 1952, in Salt Lake City, Utah. He pursued advanced education in medicine, eventually earning his medical degree and establishing himself as a respected cardiologist and physician. Before his appointment to full-time Church leadership, Renlund enjoyed a distinguished medical career, combining his professional expertise with active ecclesiastical involvement. His medical background provided him with scientific knowledge and practical experience in health and human wellbeing. In 1977, he married Ruth Lybbert, and together they established a family while balancing his demanding medical practice with significant Church responsibilities and volunteer service.
church_summary: Renlund served as a full-time missionary in Sweden from 1972 to 1974, where he developed proficiency in Scandinavian languages and culture. He was called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles in 2015. In April 2019, he dedicated the Kinshasa Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple. His ministry has emphasized religious freedom and its societal benefits, mental health and suicide prevention, religion's role in improving individual health, and youth engagement through digital platforms. His unique combination of medical knowledge and spiritual authority has allowed him to address contemporary challenges facing members, particularly regarding mental health awareness and personal wellbeing.
